questions.stem: Which prefix means 'not' or 'opposite of' when added to 'happy'?

options.option_text: pre- (pre-happy is not a standard word; pre- means before)
un- (correct: un- = not/opposite; unhappy = not happy ✓)
re- (re-happy is not a word; re- means again)
mis- (mis-happy is not a standard word; mis- means wrongly)

questions.explanation: B is correct. UN- prefix = not/opposite of. Common un- words: unhappy, unkind, unfair, unusual, uncertain, unable, unaware. Other 'not' prefixes: in-/im-/il-/ir- (incorrect, impossible, illegal, irregular); dis- (disagree, disappear); non- (nonfiction); mis- (misunderstand = understand wrongly, not 'not understand').

questions.stem: The suffix '-tion' or '-sion' converts verbs into nouns. What is the noun form of 'educate'?

options.option_text: Educating (this is a gerund/present participle, not the noun form using -tion)
Education (correct: educate + -tion = education; the verbal noun ✓)
Educative (educative = having the effect of educating; adjective suffix -ive, not noun)
Educator (educator = person who educates; agent suffix -or, not the abstract noun)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Suffix -TION/-SION converts verbs to abstract nouns: educate→education, communicate→communication, celebrate→celebration, decide→decision, conclude→conclusion. Suffix -OR/-ER = person who does: educate→educator, teach→teacher. Suffix -IVE = adjective: educate→educative.

questions.stem: The prefix 'INTER-' means 'between/among'. Which word means 'connected through a network between different entities'?

options.option_text: Intranet (INTRA- = within/inside; intranet = network within an organization)
Internet (correct: INTER- = between; internet = network between networks/organizations globally ✓)
Extranet (EXTRA- = outside; extranet = network for external authorized users)
Ultranational (ULTRA- = beyond; not related to networks)

questions.explanation: B is correct. INTER- = between/among. Internet = inter + net = between/among networks. Other INTER- words: international (between nations), interview (between viewer and viewee), interchange, intercontinental, interdependent. INTRA- = within: intranet, intramural, intrastate.

questions.stem: The suffix '-ness' forms abstract nouns. What abstract noun can be formed from 'dark'?

options.option_text: Darker (this is a comparative adjective, not an abstract noun)
Darkness (correct: dark + ness = darkness; the state or quality of being dark ✓)
Darkly (darkly = adverb suffix -ly; not an abstract noun)
Darken (darken = verb suffix -en; means to make dark)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Suffix -NESS = quality/state of being: dark→darkness, happy→happiness, sad→sadness, kind→kindness, aware→awareness. Other abstract noun suffixes: -ity (able→ability); -ment (develop→development); -ness (comparative → no noun change: darker≠darkerness).

questions.stem: The prefix 'ANTI-' means 'against'. Which word means 'a substance that works against bacteria'?

options.option_text: Probiotic (PRO- = for; probiotic = substance that promotes good bacteria)
Antibiotic (correct: ANTI- = against + biotic (relating to life/biology) = works against living bacteria ✓)
Symbiotic (SYM- = together; symbiotic = living together mutually)
Microbiotic (MICRO- = small; not specifically 'against')

questions.explanation: B is correct. ANTI- = against. Antibiotic = anti (against) + biotic (living/biological) = substance that fights bacteria. Other ANTI- words: antisocial (against social norms), antidote (against poison), anticlockwise (against clock direction), antivirus (against viruses), antibody (against foreign bodies).

questions.stem: The suffix '-ful' means 'full of'. What word means 'full of grace'?

options.option_text: Graceless (grace + less = without grace; opposite suffix)
Graceful (correct: grace + ful = graceful = having grace and elegance ✓)
Gracious (grace + ious = gracious = courteous, kind; different suffix and meaning)
Graced (grace + d = past tense of grace as verb; not the adjective)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Suffix -FUL = full of: graceful (full of grace), helpful (full of help), beautiful (full of beauty), colourful, peaceful, thankful, hopeful. Suffix -LESS = without (opposite): graceless, helpless, hopeless. These are one of the most tested suffix pairs.

questions.stem: The prefix 'OVER-' can mean 'too much/excessive'. Which word means 'too confident'?

options.option_text: Underconfident (UNDER- = too little; opposite meaning)
Overconfident (correct: OVER- = too much; overconfident = excessively confident ✓)
Unconfident (UN- = not; unconfident = not confident; not 'too much')
Misconconfident (not a standard word)

questions.explanation: B is correct. OVER- = excessive/too much: overconfident, overworked, overestimate, overweight, overreact, overflow, overload, oversleep. UNDER- = too little/insufficient: underconfident, underestimate, underweight, underpay, underperform.

questions.stem: Which suffix converts an adjective into an adverb?

options.option_text: -ment (this converts verbs to nouns: develop→development)
-ly (correct: adjective + -ly = adverb: quick→quickly, beautiful→beautifully ✓)
-ness (this converts adjectives to nouns: sad→sadness)
-ful (this converts nouns to adjectives: care→careful)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Suffix -LY converts adjectives to adverbs: quick→quickly, bright→brightly, careful→carefully, beautiful→beautifully, slow→slowly. Note: some -LY words can be adjectives too (friendly, lovely, timely). Most -LY words ending in adjective+ly are adverbs.

questions.stem: The prefix 'MIS-' means 'wrongly' or 'badly'. Which word means 'to understand wrongly'?

options.option_text: Understand (no prefix; the original verb)
Misunderstand (correct: MIS- + understand = to understand incorrectly ✓)
Overunderstand (not a real word)
Underunderstand (not a real word)

questions.explanation: B is correct. MIS- = wrongly/badly: misunderstand (understand wrongly), mislead (lead wrongly), misuse (use wrongly), misbehave (behave badly), misspell (spell wrongly), miscalculate, misjudge, misinform. This is different from UN- (which negates completely): unlike, unable.

questions.stem: The suffix '-ISM' denotes a doctrine, practice, or system. Which of these refers to belief in one God?

options.option_text: Atheism (A-THEOS-ISM = no god belief; belief that no God exists)
Polytheism (POLY-THEOS-ISM = many gods; belief in multiple gods)
Monotheism (correct: MONO-THEOS-ISM = one god; belief in one God ✓)
Pantheism (PAN-THEOS-ISM = all-god; belief that God is in everything)

questions.explanation: C is correct. MONOTHEISM = mono (one) + theos (god) + ism (belief system) = belief in one God. POLY- (many): polytheism. A- (without): atheism. PAN- (all): pantheism. Common -ISM words: capitalism, communism, socialism, nationalism, liberalism, feminism, terrorism. Each represents a system of belief or practice.
